"Case Histories" is an album by the experimental rock group Red Krayola (also known as The Red Crayola), released in 1981. Here's what I know about it:

## Background
- It was recorded with the band's leader Mayo Thompson and the group Art & Language, a British conceptual art collective
- Released on Rough Trade Records
- Part of a series of collaborations between Red Krayola and Art & Language during the late 1970s and early 1980s

## Musical Style
- Features a post-punk/art rock sound typical of Red Krayola's work from this period
- More structured and song-oriented than their earlier psychedelic work from the 1960s
- Combines angular guitar work with politically-charged, theoretical lyrics
- The music serves as a vehicle for Art & Language's conceptual and political ideas

## Content
- The lyrics are heavily influenced by Marxist theory and conceptual art discourse
- Songs often feature dense, academic language reflecting Art & Language's theoretical concerns
- Addresses themes of capitalism, art theory, and cultural criticism

## Context
- Part of the early 1980s post-punk/post-punk adjacent movement
- Released during a fertile period for experimental and politically engaged music on independent labels
- Represents an unusual fusion of conceptual art and rock music

The album is considered an important work in the intersection of conceptual art and experimental rock music, though it remained largely a cult item rather than achieving mainstream recognition.
